diagrams.title: The Map of 15 Threat Vectors
diagrams.subtitle: Click a branch: each vector is a different entry path. Highlighted concepts come from the exam objectives, not the books.

nodes.label: Vector
nodes.detail: A vector describes HOW the threat reaches the target. The family is determined by the entry path, never by the final malware.
nodes.exam: 15 families: APT, message, image, attachment, browser, network, remote access, endpoint, supply chain, external media, human, IoT, OT, physical, signal.

nodes.label: APT
nodes.detail: Advanced Persistent Threat: targeted, persistent, and well-resourced campaign combining multiple vectors.
nodes.exam: An APT is a campaign, not a single piece of malware.

nodes.label: Message-based
nodes.detail: Phishing and smishing via email, SMS, RCS, instant messaging, and collaboration tools.
nodes.exam: RCS is in the exam objectives: no book covers it.

nodes.label: Image-based
nodes.detail: QR code / quishing, embedded content, fake CAPTCHA, and deepfake: the visual hides the real action.
nodes.exam: A QR code is image-based, not signal-based.

nodes.label: Attachment-based
nodes.detail: Office macros, RTF documents, and PDFs: execution upon opening or via a link exploiting an unpatched reader.
nodes.exam: A PDF is not inherently safe.

nodes.label: Browser-based
nodes.detail: Extensions, JavaScript, password managers, cookies, and session tokens.
nodes.exam: Session hijacking bypasses MFA: the session is already authenticated.

nodes.label: Network-based
nodes.detail: Compromised routers, switches, firewalls, and virtualized appliances; theft of session keys.
nodes.exam: A trusted network device is an entry point.

nodes.label: Remote access
nodes.detail: Remote Desktop, VNC, and VPN with stolen credentials or weak configuration.
nodes.exam: An exposed VPN without MFA is a vector, not a sufficient control.

nodes.label: Endpoint-based
nodes.detail: Mobile devices, workstations, servers, tablets, trusted devices, and living-off-the-land tools.
nodes.exam: Native PowerShell = endpoint vector, detected by behavior.

nodes.label: Supply chain
nodes.detail: Compromised vendors, managed service providers, logistics providers, and trusted SaaS.
nodes.exam: A signed update distributed by the vendor is a supply chain vector.

nodes.label: External media
nodes.detail: Malicious USB drive: autorun, keylogger, or data theft on a workstation.
nodes.exam: The control is locking down USB ports and maintaining a media inventory.

nodes.label: Human-based
nodes.detail: Impersonation, contractor, visitor, spoofed biometrics, and watering hole.
nodes.exam: A watering hole compromises a site the target already visits.

nodes.label: IoT-based
nodes.detail: Connected cameras, sensors, and printers, often unmanaged and unpatched.
nodes.exam: A connected device can serve as a network entry point.

nodes.label: OT-based
nodes.detail: Operational systems and industrial networks: controllers, supervision, SCADA.
nodes.exam: OT is distinct from IoT and physical.

nodes.label: Physical-based
nodes.detail: Lock and key, access control vestibule, badges: tailgating, lost or cloned badge.
nodes.exam: A mantrap (access control vestibule) prevents tailgating by enforcing single-person entry.

nodes.label: Signal-based
nodes.detail: Proximity wireless communications: hostile Bluetooth pairing, RF injection, NFC read/write.
nodes.exam: Bluetooth, RF, and NFC are required in §2.3: none of the 4 books cover them.

quiz.question: Which vector family covers an NFC badge read by a hostile phone?
